evidence: Receiving online DO sensor: minimum observed value ~8.26 mg/L around t=118-138h, recovering to ~10.5-12.5 mg/L by t=52h; never near the 2 mg/L limit
Receiving delayed assay: P = 3.19 g/L at t=47.8h, normal growth consistent with source batches (source-1/2/3 assays: 3.02-3.06 g/L at comparable time)
physical_forward_model keep: feasible, min DO 7.67 mg/L (sensitivity 6.64-8.76), product mass 576.3 kg
physical_forward_model reduce_feed: feasible, min DO 8.70 mg/L (sensitivity 7.44-9.68), product mass 595.5 kg - higher mass than keep with greater DO margin
physical_forward_model combined: feasible, min DO 9.09 mg/L, product mass ~595.5 kg - no mass benefit over reduce_feed
submission.rationale: Stable normal observations: receiving DO never below ~8.26 mg/L (>4x the 2 mg/L hard limit) and product is growing normally (3.19 g/L at 47.8h). A stop is unnecessary. Among supported feasible plans, reduce_feed dominates KEEP: the nominal physics model predicts all sensitivity members feasible with minimum DO ~8.70 mg/L (range 7.44-9.68, far above the 2 mg/L limit) and retains ~19 kg more product mass (595.5 kg vs 576.3 kg), while also widening oxygen margin versus the keep trajectory. Combined adds aeration without any additional mass benefit over reduce_feed, and strong_feed_reduction carries unnecessary model-mismatch risk for no demonstrated gain. Chosen action: reduce_feed (0.8x feed, air unchanged).
submission.uncertainty: The physics model is a nominal source-calibrated prediction, not the hidden receiving realization; source/receiving parameter differences mean product-mass estimates carry uncalibrated error. However, the constraint margin is large (predicted minimum DO >=7.4 mg/L across all sensitivity members vs the 2 mg/L limit), so even substantial model error leaves a wide buffer against oxygen-limit violation. Sensitivity members are finite parameter perturbations, not probabilities. No physical safety guarantee is established; this is a simulated research recommendation, not equipment approval.
